# infrawrench_custom_graph (Resource)

A code-defined graph: TypeScript that queries the organization's data and returns a series to chart.

This is the resource where Terraform earns its keep most obviously. The graph is source code, so it belongs beside the rest of your source code — `source = file("${path.module}/graphs/burn.ts")` keeps it in the repository, under review, with a diff you can read, instead of in a web editor where the last edit has no author and no history.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The graph is source code, so it lives beside the rest of your source code
# rather than in a web editor where the last edit has no author and no history.
resource "infrawrench_custom_graph" "burn" {
  name        = "Platform burn"
  description = "Spend per day against the platform team's budget."
  source      = file("${path.module}/graphs/burn.ts")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name, 1–120 characters.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the graph shows, up to 500 characters.
- `source` (String) The graph's TypeScript, up to 128 KiB. Use `file()` rather than a heredoc.

It is **not** type-checked at plan time: the API's checker is a separate route this provider does not call, because a plan that hit it would need the code to compile before Terraform had told you what it was about to change. A graph whose source does not compile is stored and fails when rendered.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned graph id. Use it with `terraform import`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the object in the app, and in the
# --json output of the Infrawrench CLI.
terraform import infrawrench_custom_graph.example 1f2a3b4c-5d6e-7f8a-9b0c-1d2e3f4a5b6c
```
